component.name: Moonglow Toolset
component.summary: Build modules for Neverwinter Nights: Enhanced Edition

description.p: Moonglow is a module toolset for Neverwinter Nights: Enhanced Edition, a reimplementation of BioWare's Aurora Toolset that runs on Linux, Windows and macOS. It edits what Aurora edits: areas with their tiles and objects, blueprints and palettes, conversations, journals, factions, scripts and module properties, and builds, verifies and tests the module in the game.
Moonglow reads the game's data from your installation; it needs a copy of Neverwinter Nights: Enhanced Edition.

Object Walkmeshes no longer throws a spike across the area view when the camera passes a tall or hanging placeable. Compile All Scripts skips the scripts that are unchanged, Compile Models uses every core, and Export as Files can write compiled models as text.

Models kept as text can be compiled (the hak editor's Compile Models, mg pack --compile-models), compiled models are shown and saved as text, and Verify Module reads text models as the game would. Menus open by their letters, the module tree has more keys, Find References answers at once after its first question, and scripts that include a changed script are compiled with it.

Cut-out textures (leaves, fences, grass) keep the edges the game gives them: cut at the game's own threshold and solid above it. A script saved in another editor is compiled when Moonglow reads it again, and the haks and content folders are watched for changes without holding the window.
A material that says twosided is drawn from behind too, as the game draws it: leaves, cloth and other thin surfaces no longer vanish seen from their back.

Fog and other particle effects with a flip-book texture play its frames in the game's order (a fog placeable showed as bright streaks), and Linked particle ribbons are as wide as the game's. The window no longer stalls every few seconds with a large module folder or nasher project open.

A module folder is worked on in place, as in Aurora: files saved, added or deleted in it by another program (scripts kept open in an editor of your own) are read again, and a save in Moonglow never writes over them.

The window by the keyboard: the menus (Alt or F10, the arrows, Enter), the tabs (Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+Shift+T) and the module tree. A View menu folds the module tree, the palettes and the log away and brings them back. The palette's header is regrouped: the types as a row of icons, one toolbar over the list. A window opens where one of its kind was last docked. A code review's fixes: less work every frame, and a dozen small faults.

A waterfall's water falls (in Medieval Rural it ran back up the stream). Export Files, over a model's picture, writes the files the game draws a placeable, door, item or creature with (models, walkmeshes, textures, materials) from the haks into a folder; mg model-files does the same from a terminal.

A module whose hak has an encoding.2da (a language the game has no letters for, such as Turkish) is read and written by it, in the toolset, in plugins and in mg. A module folder with one resource under two spellings (x.UTI and x.uti) is one file after a save. mg roundtrip checks that a module comes back as it was. A creature's selection box is around it as it stands; a palette's rows are one line; Update Instances lists what it updated; a special ability has one switch, Ready.

Names in the game's DM Creator and in Aurora's Custom palette are no longer garbled after a save: open a module and save it once to repair it. Ctrl + wheel scales what is selected; the arrow keys move through the palette; the hak list of Module Properties is reordered by a drag or the keys; Update Instances reaches items in containers; the Talk Table editor has Go to; a module folder is also saved as a .mod.
A cloak lying in an area is drawn as the game draws it: folded, in the cloak's colors, where Moonglow drew a bag.

Triggers and encounters turn by their outlines, alone and with a group. The Shaft of Light's beam stands upright. Export can add to an archive that is already there. The talk table editor reads and writes JSON, hides empty lines and opens .tlk files on their own; the resource browser exports what it lists as files.

A body part of an elf, halfling or other race that has no texture of its own name is drawn in the human's of that name, as the game draws it: clothes on such creatures no longer show another part's texture.

Lights: Add Light Here on an area's right-click menu places one of the game's invisible lights, shown as a small sun with a ring for its reach. Body parts are drawn in their own textures, as the game draws them; Raise/Lower stays in hand on a right click that finds no ground; on Windows a maximized window no longer seems to start twice.

The debug log is written unless switched off, a file for each start with the time on each line, the last five kept: what led to a crash is there to send afterwards. Items lie in an area as the game lays them, armor as its dropped model; the tiles that refuse a terrain stroke flash red; a test can start the game without Steam.

Text typed in another language than English keeps its letters; conversation lines are dropped above one another and have a right-click menu; an encounter's spawn points move on their own; several objects turn together about their middle; Resize Area at any two edges; a tile's variants are chosen by picture in Tile Properties, now a window to resize and dock.

No key moves the area's camera while text is typed in a window over it; Edit on the module tree's right-click menus; the Build Module window keeps its size with Advanced Controls; a creature's environment map is not reflected through a material whose shader switches it off.

A script editor opens other scripts, the module's, a hak's or the game's; the module tree shows the object selected in the area and keeps its filter in sight; New in the palettes' menus; a creature's assigned feats are listed; armor and cloaks lying in an area draw as the game draws them; palette categories named only in the older field keep their names; animations bind by part number.

Scripts are compiled when the module is saved, where that is asked for; a nasher project's script opens in place in the external editor; text shows in English where the language edited has none; the module tree goes to the area of the tab chosen.

Static placeables stand upright and a TGA's right-to-left flag is ignored, as in the game; tokens go in at the caret; a marker before fields that differ among what is edited together; the keys exported and imported; more of the terrain for plugins.

Plugins can read a file or folder you choose, write haks you allow, make areas and paint terrain; a folder of tileset files is imported as a hak and an area; two community tileset shaders (vertex-colored and blended layers, lightmaps) are drawn.
A click lands on an object's model, not its box; fog and other slow emitters show at once in the area; the Eraser takes a tile group away whole; a project file that isn't UTF-8 opens.

An external script compiler can be chosen; Steam Workshop content is read, and the game is found in other Steam libraries; the grid shows red from the area's edge; include files are no longer compiled on their own.

Inventories are dragged, copied and pasted, and an item's Properties open from them; the Appearance Gallery has creatures and doors; an item's model shows in its Appearance page, armor and cloaks on a man or a woman; Fade Geometry has Aurora's three choices; the Options are a tab.
The galleries' pictures of things made for a wall are no longer blank; an appearance dragged into the area shows where it would go.
The galleries' names are easier to read; a picture dragged from the Placeable Gallery into the area places a placeable; panes have their margin back.

Galleries: the palette shows blueprints as pictures, and the Placeable Gallery every placeable appearance, to give to what is selected with a click. Water moves. A round of builders' reports: copy and paste on Windows, sounds that come up gradually, windows that keep their size, any snapping angle, Escape to deselect.
Fixes cloaks drawn over the face of elves and other bodies that aren't a human's size. On Windows, a zip of the programs beside the installer, which Scoop installs.

A handle scales a selected object's model in the area view; tiles show their particles (a chimney's smoke, with its animation loop on); Shift leaves the camera alone while the handles show (Alt turns the selection and moves the camera); dialogs open in the middle of the window. On Windows, Scoop can install and update Moonglow.
Fixes blue-white patches round plants and along shores in the area view, seen at a slant. The area view's readout names the tile under the pointer.

The module tree can no longer take the whole window. A nasher project's files changed by another program are read again while it is open. A debug log for problems that fail without a word. Windows remember their size and maximize. The game's text and tokens in the language edited.

Custom creatures from the Vault and CEP are drawn right: scaled models, bodies without some parts, heads and dragons that showed untextured, torn skins. Pale rims round transparent textures are gone. Edit beside a script's name makes a script that doesn't exist yet. Expand All and Collapse All in the module tree and the palettes.

The start location's marker is dragged and turned in the area view. Delete on a resource in the module tree, an area with everything placed in it. The Loading Screen choice shows each screen's picture.

Set the start location from an area's menu. Palette categories of your own, added, renamed and dragged into order. The module tree lists what is placed in each area. Prefabs on the area's toolbar and in the palette. Descriptions of skills, feats and spells on hover. A model that fails is left out rather than ending the toolset.

Fixes a crash on loading a module with a model whose skin names bones it doesn't have, Options closing the open module, and dropdowns closing when their Filter field is clicked. Talk tables go to and from CSV; the hak editor sorts, views resources and updates from its folder; placeable, door and item pages show the model; a spawn point's facing is turned in the area view.

Make Placeables Static sets Static on an area's or the module's placeables that lose nothing by it. Textures saved with a top-left origin (by Krita) show as in the game. An Animations switch holds creatures still in the area view. The script editor fills its pane and its lists open wide enough for their names.

With Shift held, the selected object in the area view shows two rings that tilt its model and three arrows that move it along one axis alone. A placeable's menu makes it static or dynamic. A module opens on the area you opened last in it.

A turning ring around the selected object in the area view: take it anywhere and lead it round to turn the selection (Options, Area switches it off). An object held while the middle button swings the camera stays in hand when that button is let go, and Escape drops a drag.

From builders' reviews: the fields view names what a number stands for (an area's music, a creature's feats); the module tree lists blueprints by name and makes new ones from its menus; feats and spells are found by category; special abilities are uses of a spell; a creature's model shows in its Appearance page; encounters' spawn points show their facing; a light theme and an interface size.

Files out of the toolset: To Scratch in the script editor (the script compiled, with its compiled script) and the area view copies loose files into a folder of your choice, such as a server's development folder; Export as Files and Copy to Scratch Folder in the module tree; mg export --files from the command line.

Plugins (experimental): commands and checks of your own, written in Luau and run in a sandbox, installed from a file and off until enabled; their edits are one step of Undo, and their checks run with Verify Module. The plugin API is at 0.1 and may still change. The Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) finds any command, and every menu command can be given a key. Compile All Scripts, Build Module and Verify Module run in the background, with progress and Cancel. mg set and mg apply change a module's fields from the command line.

Several areas' properties are edited together: Edit Areas Together lists the module's areas to tick, by name, tileset and kind, and sets their lighting, fog, weather, music, scripts and variables at once; mg areas does the same from the command line. Variables edited for several objects merge into each. Forms have ruled headings, and labels in the regular face.

Merchants and sounds are hidden by what stands in front of them: they were drawn over the view. Merchants stay yellow arrows, or the game's $ sign (Options, Area); sounds are the game's markers for them. The Variables window's name field shows a whole name.

Waypoints show the flags of their appearance; the area view draws the ranges of placed sounds, lights a dark area evenly with its lighting switched off, and moves its camera up and down (Z and C, or Ctrl + Shift with the wheel or a middle drag); areas can be listed by name rather than ResRef; the Options window keeps its size; and the cliffs of the Forest - Facelift tileset are drawn whole.

Areas on custom tilesets whose door counts are no counts (values left by the editor that wrote them) open again: Moonglow froze on them, its memory growing. A tileset with a group missing loads; Area Properties reads the tileset once, not on every frame.

An armor's parts take colors of their own (the game's per-part colors, which Aurora has no page for), edited on the item's Appearance page and shown in previews; the Eraser drags as terrain brushes do; a body part whose model names a missing texture is drawn with its own.

Painting terrain shows the tiles a click or a drag will make before it is made; drags fill a rectangle or follow its outline with Shift and let go of what they pass when run back; a Refine Tile tool steps a tile through those that fit. Blueprints show where they will be placed and turn with Q and E; merchants preview what they sell; tabs rename what they show; and the editors use the whole window, with bold labels.

JSON output from every command-line tool, and mg find and mg info for questions about a module; NWSync publishing (Build › Publish to NWSync… and mg nwsync), as nwn_nwsync_write publishes; a tileset editor that changes only the lines it edits, makes the tileset's palette and renders its minimap pictures.

Palettes find blueprints by tag and close matches, show a picture on hover, and keep favorites and recent ones; a talk-table editor and 2DAs shown with their text and the hak each row comes from; a hak editor, and haks and a talk table attached to a module in one step; placeable and door walkmeshes in the area view, and minimaps exported as the game draws them; keys that can be changed in Options.

Modules as nasher projects for git; Find References and Rename everywhere; Verify names what crashes Aurora in custom content; Test From Here and reloading changed haks; placement tools and prefabs; go to definition, references, renaming and live errors in scripts, and an NWScript language server; fields for EE data Aurora hides; bulk edits and Find and Replace; conversations that play as the game plays them and go out to and come back from text, CSV, Twine and Ink.

Editors open in windows over the area view; blueprints drag from the palette into areas; previews follow their editors and show placed objects; the camera turns with a right drag and moves with W, A, S and D; layout and usability fixes throughout.
First release: functional parity with the Aurora Toolset.
